all GABA agonists studied in the crayfish SRN act by the same cooperative allosteric mechanism, that GABA uptake processes can influence the apparent affinity and cooperativity of GABA receptors, but not the affinity and cooperativity for other GABA agonists, and that the crayfish SRNs can be a useful tool to quantitate the effects of GABA receptor agonists.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the GABA receptor-ionophore units of the crayfish SRN and mammalian brain are similar in that both exhibit a cooperative interaction with GABA and related agonists, and that the GABA uptake processes in the SRN can be blocked by several compounds which are also known to block the GABA uptake system in mammalian brain.

the crayfish SRN is a very useful preparation for the study of GABA receptor function, and that the SRN is a useful model system for the study of the interaction of GABA and GABA agonists with GABA receptors.

the GABA receptor-ionophore complex of the SRN is very similar to that found in mammalian brain, and that the SRN may be a useful model for studying the interaction of GABA and its analogs with the GABA receptor complex.
